tools.name: vectorcraft_command_list
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Discover command ids, labels, parameter descriptions and enabled state. Returns an array.

filter.description: Case-insensitive id, label or menu substring

tools.name: vectorcraft_command_run
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Run an engine command by id with its JSON params. Command parameters follow the registry's descriptions.

tools.name: vectorcraft_command_batch
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Run steps in order; each edit is its own undo step, or with atomic:true the whole batch is one (named `label`, else after its first edit). A param string that is exactly "$N.path" (N: 0-based step index) or "$last.path" takes that value from an earlier step's result, e.g. {"id":"$1.id"}; "$$" starts a literal "$". Returns completed, failed and results. Stops on the first error by default.

atomic.description: Make the batch's edits one undo step (needs an open document)

label.description: The undo step's name with atomic

tools.name: vectorcraft_doc_inspect
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Summary of the active document, including artboards, layer tree, selection and history.

tools.name: vectorcraft_render_preview
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Render an artboard (default the first) as inline PNG without changing the document. max_side defaults to 1024, limited to 1..4096.

tools.name: vectorcraft_ui_inspect
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Inspect the connected desktop interface; returns a tool error in headless mode.

tools.name: vectorcraft_ui_screenshot
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Capture the connected desktop window as inline PNG; requires a running desktop app.

tools.name: vectorcraft_list_commands
tools.description: [vectorcraft] List VectorCraft commands (id, label, menu path, shortcut, parameter description, enabled state). Every editing action is a command; run any of them with run_command. Coordinates are points in document space, y down, origin at the first artboard's top-left.

enabledOnly.description: Only commands that can run right now

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against id, label and menu path (e.g. "align", "Object")

tools.name: vectorcraft_run_command
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Execute any VectorCraft command by id with JSON params (see list_commands for ids and params). Examples: {"command":"object.group"}, {"command":"object.align","params":{"horizontal":"left"}}, {"command":"file.new","params":{"width":800,"height":600}}. Returns the command's result (e.g. {id} for creation commands).

command.description: Command id, e.g. shape.rectangle, object.group, paint.setFill

tools.name: vectorcraft_inspect_document
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Summary of the active document: artboards, layer tree (ids, names, kinds, bounds, fill/stroke), selection, undo history, current tool and default paint. On a large document pass depth: 0 for the layer skeleton (truncated levels report childCount), then locate objects with run_command document.find and read them with document.node.

childLimit.description: Children shown per node (default all; a level that shows fewer reports childCount)

depth.description: Child levels of the layer tree to include (default all; 0 = top layers with counts)

tools.name: vectorcraft_inspect_ui
tools.description: [vectorcraft] UI state of the running desktop app: tool and options, panels, dialogs, view (zoom/center), window, documents, perf. Desktop app only.

tools.name: vectorcraft_select_tool
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Switch the active tool (as clicking it in the Tools panel). Ids: selection, directSelection, groupSelection, pen, rectangle, roundedRectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, lineSegment, …

tools.name: vectorcraft_pointer_gesture
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Drive the active tool with mouse events in document coordinates, exactly like the mouse would (e.g. a rectangle drag: down at (100,100), drag to (200,150), up at (200,150)). Optionally selects `tool` first.

holdMs.description: Milliseconds the pointer then holds still, button down (0..60000): Twirl, Pucker and Bloat keep applying

mods.description: Modifier keys held (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)

pressure.description: Pen pressure 0..1 (default 1): the Liquify tools' intensity with Use Pressure Pen on

mods.description: Modifier keys held (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)

tool.description: Optional tool to select before the gesture

tools.name: vectorcraft_draw_path
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Create a path from points ([[x,y],…] or [{x,y,in?:[x,y],out?:[x,y]},…] with Bézier handles) or SVG path data `d`, then apply optional paint. Omitted paint fields inherit the current new-art appearance (initially white fill and 1 pt black stroke). For a filled path without an outline, pass an explicit fill and stroke:"none". Returns the new object id.

d.description: SVG path data (alternative to points), e.g. "M0 0 L100 0 L50 80 Z"

fill.description: Fill: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

points.description: Anchors: [x,y] pairs or {x, y, in?, out?, smooth?} objects

stroke.description: Stroke: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

tools.name: vectorcraft_draw_shape
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Create a live shape and apply optional paint. rectangle/ellipse: x, y, width, height (rectangle: radius = corner radius). polygon: cx, cy, radius, sides. star: cx, cy, radius1, radius2, points. line: x1, y1, x2, y2. Omitted paint fields inherit the current new-art appearance (initially white fill and 1 pt black stroke); lines start with no fill and a visible stroke. For a filled shape without an outline, pass an explicit fill and stroke:"none". Returns the new object id.

fill.description: Fill: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

stroke.description: Stroke: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

tools.name: vectorcraft_set_paint
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Set fill, stroke and/or stroke weight on the selection (or `ids`) and as the default for new art.

fill.description: Fill: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

stroke.description: Stroke: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

tools.name: vectorcraft_press_key
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Send a key press with modifiers, e.g. {key:"Z", mods:{cmd:true}} (undo), {key:"Escape"}, {key:"Enter"}. In the desktop app it goes through the real keyboard path; headless, it runs the command or tool bound to that shortcut.

key.description: Key name: A–Z, 0–9, Enter, Escape, Delete, Backspace, Tab, Space, Left/Right/Up/Down, [ ]…

mods.description: Modifier keys held (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)

tools.name: vectorcraft_type_text
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Type text into the focused widget (text tool, dialog field). Desktop app only.

tools.name: vectorcraft_invoke_menu
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Invoke a menu item by its command id (same ids as list_commands, including UI-only commands like view.zoomIn or window.* in the desktop app).

tools.name: vectorcraft_open_panel
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Open a panel in the desktop app's dock by id (layers, swatches, stroke, align, pathfinder, transform, …; case-insensitive, display labels like "Layers" work too). Desktop app only.

tools.name: vectorcraft_screenshot
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Render the active artboard to PNG and return it as an image (optionally also saving it to `path`). With window:true (desktop app only) captures the whole app window instead.

window.description: Capture the app window (desktop app only)

tools.name: vectorcraft_open_file
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Open a file as a new, active document: .vectorcraft, .drawcraft, .svg, .svgz, .pdf, .ai, .ait, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .tif, .tiff, .bmp, .psd, .psb, .vctemplate, .dxf, .emf, .wmf, .eps, .af, .afdesign, .afpub (see run_command document.formats). Templates (.ait, native templates) open as a new untitled document. The reply's `warnings` say what didn't come in as it was (an EPS shown as its preview image says why its PostScript couldn't be read).

tools.name: vectorcraft_save_file
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Save the active document with the engine's document.save: by default to its own file in its own format (native .vectorcraft unless it was opened from or saved as SVG, PDF or a restorable .ai). With `path`, the extension picks the format: .vectorcraft, .vctemplate, .pdf, .svg, .svgz, .ai. Other formats are exports (see export). The reply's `format` says what was written and `warnings` what that format loses.

path.description: Destination; its extension picks the format (default: the document's own file)

tools.name: vectorcraft_export
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Export the active document with the engine's document.export (the same bytes in the app and headless), in any format of the `format` enum: vectors (svg/svgz with the artboard as viewBox, eps, dxf, emf, wmf), pdf (one page per artboard: all, or `artboard` / `range`), rasters (one rendered artboard: png, jpg, webp, gif, png8 as an indexed .png, tiff, bmp, tga, psd with its layers), txt (the stories, back to front), vectorcraft or template (a native copy or template; the document keeps its path). run_command document.formats lists each format's options. For SVG/SVGZ, top-level `outlineText: true` writes text as paths; DXF takes it too (its type is outlined anyway unless `preserve: editability`). PDF instead uses `options.advanced.outlineText: true`, default false (live text). `selection: true` exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds. Template layers are left out; live effects are kept (geometry baked, SVG filters for shadows/glows/blur). Without `path` the bytes come back as dataBase64.

artboard.description: 0-based artboard (default: the first; PDF default: all)

options.description: More format options, passed through (see run_command document.formats), e.g. {"quality": 80} for jpg or {"advanced": {"outlineText": true}} for PDF text as outlines (default false: live text)

outlineText.description: SVG/SVGZ: true writes text as outlines (viewable without the fonts). DXF takes it too (type outlined anyway unless preserve: editability). PDF uses options.advanced.outlineText instead (default false: live text)

range.description: 1-based artboards such as "1-3, 5" (PDF: one page each; other formats take one)

selection.description: Export only the selection, cropped to it

tools.name: vectorcraft_add_text
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Create point type at (x, y) (the first baseline), area type when width/height are given, or type in/on an existing path (`path` id + `mode` area|onPath; `pathEffect` rainbow|skew|3dRibbon|stairStep|gravity). Returns the text object id.

color.description: Text colour (#rrggbb): "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

path.description: Existing path id to flow the text in (area) or along (onPath)

tools.name: vectorcraft_apply_effect
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Append a live effect (Effect menu) to the selection or `ids`. Omit `effect` to get the catalogue (ids, parameters, defaults). Examples: stylize.dropShadow {x, y, blur, opacity}, distort.roughen, warp.arc {bend}, path.offsetPath {offset}, pathfinder.add (on groups), blur.gaussian {radius}.

params.description: Effect parameters; missing keys take the dialog defaults

tools.name: vectorcraft_pathfinder
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Combine the selected (or `ids`) objects destructively, back to front: unite, minusFront, intersect, exclude, divide, trim, merge, crop, outline, minusBack. For a non-destructive version apply the pathfinder.* effect to a group.

tools.name: vectorcraft_transform
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Move, rotate, scale, reflect or shear the selection (or `ids`); several may be combined and run in that order. Angles in degrees (counter-clockwise), scale in %. `origin` [x,y] defaults to the selection centre; `copy` transforms a copy.

tools.name: vectorcraft_create_graph
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Create a graph (graph tools) in the plot rectangle. Data as `csv` (first row: empty cell then series names; then one row per category: label, values…) or `series`/`categories`/`rows`. An empty CSV cell or a null in `rows` is a blank value (no column; lines break around it); a number in straight quotes is a label. Edit later with run_command graph.setData / graph.setType.

tools.name: vectorcraft_text_wrap
tools.description: [vectorcraft] Make the selected (or `ids`) objects wrap objects: area type below them in the same layer flows around them (offset in pt, invert = flow inside). `release: true` removes the wrap.

offset.description: Gap between text and object (default 6 pt)

tools.description:
[vectorcraft] Paste
Location: Edit
Shortcut: Cmd+V
Params doc: {center?: [x, y], dx?, dy?, swatchConflict?} paste centred on `center` (the app passes the view centre), else offset by dx/dy (default: the Paste Offset preference). Pasting brings the image blobs, symbols, patterns, global and spot swatches (with the tint swatches of the tints used), gradient swatches, graphic styles, character and paragraph styles and brushes the objects use; one of the same name that differs comes in renamed. swatchConflict, for a swatch whose name the document gives another colour (clipboard.conflicts): "merge" (default: the objects take the document's swatch) | "add" (the pasted swatch comes in renamed) | {name: "merge"|"add"}. With Paste Remembers Layers on (layer.pasteRemembersLayers), objects go back into the layers they came from (by name; made when missing). An artboard copied with artboard.copy comes with its art, right of the last artboard (the other paste commands but Paste on All Artboards: where it was), its art back in the layers it came from → {ids, artboard: the new artboard's index or null, added: resources added, merged: conflicts merged, renamed: [{kind, from, to}]}

(encrypted PDFs; see document.pdfInfo), textAs?: text (default: point type per line, lines wrapped in a frame as area type where they lay out the same, in the file's fonts by name; missing ones are listed in warnings) | outlines (glyph paths), layers?: true (default: optional content groups become layers with their visibility, print state and lock — art that is off comes in as a hidden layer; other art goes to a layer per page) | false (one layer per page, without the art that is off; Save then asks for a name), editingData?: true (default: an EPS, .ai or PDF that carries its editor's own copy of the art opens from it, with its layers, hidden objects, guides, artboards and the art outside them; a .ai or PDF whose type shows opens from its PDF part with textAs: outlines) | false (only what its page or PDF part prints, for print pipelines; a .ai saved without PDF compatibility then can't be opened), colorMode?: rgb|cmyk (the mode the document opens in, its colours converted as file.documentColorMode does, grays? as there; default: the file's — a PDF keeps CMYK, Gray and spot inks (spot swatches at a tint) and opens in CMYK when painted mostly in CMYK), DXF: dxf?: {layout?: "Model" (default) | a paper layout's name (document.dxfInfo lists them), unit?, scale? (the ratio: 1 unit of the art = scale drawing units; default: the drawing at 1:1 in its own unit), fit?: false (scale to fit an artboard of fitTo?: [612, 792], turned to the art's orientation), scaleLineweights?: false (lineweights scale with the art), center?: true (false: the drawing's origin on the artboard's bottom-left corner; fitted art's bottom-left corner), mergeLayers?: false (all art on one layer)} → {index, title, format, warnings, restored, missingLinks, modifiedLinks, updatedLinks: [{name, path, ids}]}; any readable format (see document.formats): .vectorcraft/.drawcraft, .svg/.svgz, .pdf/.ai, .ait, ASCII .dxf (each DXF layer with art a layer; blocks symbols; what can't come in is listed in warnings), PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/TIFF/BMP (an image opens as a document of its size at the resolution it declares, as file.place sizes it; 72 ppi, 1 px = 1 pt, when it declares none), .emf/.wmf (one artboard, the picture's frame; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning), .eps and PostScript .ai (one artboard, the bounding box: an EPS file VectorCraft wrote restores the document it carries, restored: true; other files are read by a PostScript interpreter — paths, colours and spot inks, clips, gradients, images, type in the fonts named — and come in as their TIFF preview, with a warning, when their PostScript can't be read). [vectorcraft] Find Linked Files
Params doc: {folder?: an absolute path, ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the active document's missing links), maxSeconds?: 60 (1 to 600), stop?: false (true: stop the last search)} with folder: look in it and its subfolders, on separate threads, for files with the names of the linked files (in any letter case), and answer at once with the search's state (searching while it runs); without folder: the last search's state, with the files found so far. Each linked file's files come best first: same (the size and hash saved with the link), size (the saved size, where there is no saved hash or the file is larger than 1 GB), then name. Within each kind, a file whose name has the link's letter case comes first. Then each file's folder names are compared with the saved path's, from the innermost outward up to the first one that differs, and a file with more matching names comes first; files that still tie are listed by path. A search looks for at most 1000 linked files and keeps the first 10 files of each one's name, and up to 10 that are the same file; it ends once every linked file has its same file, and searches only the folders text.findFontFiles may search, with the same maxSeconds, depth and count limits; none on the web → {id (absent while idle), state: idle|searching|done|stopped|failed, folder?, links: [{name, path, ids, files: [{path, size, match: same|size|name, caseDiffers?: true}]}], searched?: {folders, files, read}, skipped?, unreadable?, stopped?: stop|time|limit, error?, seconds?}
